## What to build

The measurement harness for the ranking ship decision, fully buildable without owner time:

1. A committed query set of 30 to 50 investigation-style queries with rationale per category: company events, macro and rates, commodities, multi-day live-blog stories, paraphrase pairs (same information need, different wording), ticker-style queries (stemming stress), and negative controls the corpus should not answer.
2. A pooled-run driver: execute both rankers (`mode: bm25` and `mode: weighted`) per query, form the deduplicated union of each ranker's top 20 chunks, blinded so the grader cannot tell which ranker surfaced a chunk.
3. Labeling panel wiring: each pooled chunk is graded 0 (irrelevant), 1 (related context), or 2 (answers the query), with full chunk text and a source link visible.
4. An nDCG@10 scorer that reads the labels and reports per-query and mean scores per ranker.

Deterministic and re-runnable: same labels in, same numbers out. Labels persist additively (id-keyed) so a second session never destroys the first.

In `mode: 'weighted'`, ranking depends on tier/aggregator/quality/recency, none of which the SQL bm25-order pagination can account for, so `retrieve.ts` fetches every matching row unbounded (`limit: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, already a supported store.ts sentinel), scores all of them, sorts by score desc (same chunk_ref tie-break), then slices the requested page out of the fully-ordered set. This is the only way pagination is correct in weighted mode; the cost (O(matching rows) instead of O(page size) per call) only applies once weighted mode ships (R4/#227), never in the bm25 shipping default.
